theorem.statement:
Fix \(r\in\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), put
\[
 \nu=\min\{1,\delta/R_{\max}\},
 \qquad
 \varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}=\frac{\nu}{8+4\nu},
\]
and let \(0<\chi<\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}\) and \(m_n\to\infty\) be deterministic.  The randomized-jitter Gaussian-multiplier set \(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\) is implementable from the stratified observations and auxiliary standard normal draws.  Uniformly over every triangular array in \(\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)\),
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)}
 \left|
 \Pr_\theta\{\beta\in\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\}
 -(1-\alpha_0)
 \right|=0,
\]
where the probability is unconditional over the observations, all Gaussian multipliers, the observed-statistic jitter, and all Monte Carlo jitters.  The conclusion allows the same-sample estimated-\(A\) influence covariance \(\Sigma_n\) to be singular, to change rank with \(n\), or to equal zero, and it uses neither a covariance inverse nor a positive-eigenvalue bound.  Since \(\tau_n=n^{-\chi}\to0\), the randomization vanishes on the root-\(n\) projected-moment scale underlying \(\mathcal C_n\); the displayed limit is therefore exact, rather than conservative, null calibration of an Anderson--Rubin inversion.

There is a precise atomic limitation for deterministic single-threshold calibration.  If a reference statistic has distribution function \(F\), has an atom at a proposed cutoff \(x_0\), and
\[
 F(x_0-)<1-\alpha_0<F(x_0),
\]
then neither the deterministic rule accepting below \(x_0\) nor the deterministic rule accepting at or below \(x_0\) has acceptance probability \(1-\alpha_0\).  This limitation concerns those deterministic single-threshold conventions at an atom; it is not an impossibility claim about every procedure without external randomization.
theorem.proof_tex:
Write \(\mathcal K=\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\), and use the block maximum norm from the construction.  Its dimension \(D_{\mathrm{AR}}=(E-1)(R_{\max}-d-1)\) is fixed.  All constants below depend only on the fixed coefficient, moment, share, and calibration-gap envelopes.  In particular, they are independent of the member of the triangular array.

By balanced shares, \(n_e\geq\underline\pi n\).  Thus \(n_e\geq R_{\max}\) for every environment when \(n\) is sufficiently large, so the small-sample fallback is well defined and eventually inactive.  At the true value \(b=\beta\), the uniform generated-projector expansion gives
\[
 H_n(\beta)=Z_n+R_n,
 \qquad
 Z_n=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
 \pi_e^{-1}\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i}),
 \tag{1}
\]
where \(R_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly and
\[
 \Sigma_n=\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\pi_e^{-1}
 \mathbb E[\zeta_{e,n}\zeta_{e,n}^{\top}].
 \tag{2}
\]
The proof of that expansion constructs each coordinate of \(\zeta_{e,n}\) from cumulant first projections of polynomial degree at most \(R_{\max}\), the projector \(Q_A\), the pseudoinverse \(C^+\), and bounded population cumulants.  The moment envelope, the coefficient bounds inherited through the ambient class, and the calibration gap \(\|C^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa_0^{-1}\) therefore imply, for
\[
 \nu=\min\{1,\delta/R_{\max}\}>0,
\]
that
\[
 \sup_{n,e,\theta}
 \mathbb E_\theta\|\zeta_{e,n}\|^{2+\nu}\leq K.
 \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, the required source moment order is at most \((2+\nu)R_{\max}\leq2R_{\max}+\delta\), exactly the order supplied by the moment envelope.  The division by the smallest calibration singular value is licensed by \(\sigma_d(C)\geq\kappa_0>0\).

We first quantify the Gaussian approximation without dividing by an eigenvalue.  Put
\[
 X_{e,i,n}=n^{-1/2}\pi_e^{-1}\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i}).
\]
Balanced shares and (3) give
\[
 \sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
 \mathbb E\|X_{e,i,n}\|^{2+\nu}
 \leq K n^{-\nu/2}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Let \(f\) be bounded by one and one-Lipschitz, and let \(f_s\) be its convolution with the \(N(0,s^2I_{D_{\mathrm{AR}}})\) density.  Translation coupling gives
\[
 \|f_s-f\|_\infty\leq K s.
\]
Differentiating the Gaussian density twice and subtracting the value of \(f\) at the convolution center gives
\[
 [D^2f_s]_{\nu}\leq K s^{-1-\nu}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Replace the independent summands \(X_{e,i,n}\), one at a time, by independent centered Gaussian vectors with the same covariances.  Taylor's formula through order two cancels the mean and covariance terms.  Its integral remainder and (5) bound the error for one replacement by a constant times \(s^{-1-\nu}\) times the sum of the \((2+\nu)\)-moments of the original and Gaussian summands.  If \(G\) is the corresponding Gaussian summand, then
\[
 \mathbb E\|G\|^{2+\nu}
 \leq K\{\mathbb E\|X_{e,i,n}\|^2\}^{1+\nu/2}
 \leq K\mathbb E\|X_{e,i,n}\|^{2+\nu},
\]
where the first inequality uses fixed dimensionality and the second is Lyapunov's inequality.  Summing the replacements and using (4) yields
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\bigl(\mathcal L(Z_n),N(0,\Sigma_n)\bigr)
 \leq K\{s+n^{-\nu/2}s^{-1-\nu}\}.
\]
With \(s=n^{-\nu/(4+2\nu)}\),
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\bigl(\mathcal L(Z_n),N(0,\Sigma_n)\bigr)
 \leq K n^{-\nu/(4+2\nu)}.
 \tag{6}
\]
No step uses nonsingularity of \(\Sigma_n\).

We also need a rate for the expansion remainder in (1).  The overlap count for a canonical Hoeffding projection of order \(j\geq2\) gives mean square \(O(n_e^{-j})\) before root-\(n\) scaling, and hence at most \(O(n^{-1})\) after multiplication by \(\sqrt n\), using balanced shares.  The rank-\(d\) projector expansion has remainder bounded by \(K\sqrt n\|\widehat C-C\|^2\) on
\(\{\|\widehat C-C\|\leq\kappa_0/2\}\).  The first-projection variance calculation gives
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widehat C-C\|^2\leq K/n,
 \qquad
 \Pr\{\|\widehat C-C\|>\kappa_0/2\}\leq K/n.
 \tag{7}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[1\wedge
 \{\sqrt n\|\widehat C-C\|^2\}\right]
 \leq K n^{-1/2}.
\]
Every product of two first-order estimation errors has the same truncated-mean bound by Cauchy--Schwarz and their \(O(n^{-1})\) mean squared errors.  Combining these bounds with the canonical-projection bound and the exceptional probability in (7) gives
\[
 \sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta[1\wedge\|R_n\|]
 \leq K n^{-1/2}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Since a bounded one-Lipschitz function changes by at most \(1\wedge\|R_n\|\), (6)--(8), and \(\nu\leq1\), imply
\[
 \sup_\theta d_{\mathrm{BL}}
 \bigl(\mathcal L_\theta(H_n(\beta)),N(0,\Sigma_n)\bigr)
 \leq K n^{-\nu/(4+2\nu)}.
 \tag{9}
\]

We next prove the quantitative estimated-influence replacement bound.  This is the step for which convergence merely in probability would not suffice.  For an order-\(s\) constituent kernel \(g\), let
\[
 \psi_{g,e}(w)=s\{\mathbb E[g(w,W_2,\ldots,W_s)]-\mathbb E g\}.
\]
If \(s=1\), the first average in \(\widehat\psi_{g,e,i}\) is \(g(W_{e,i})\) itself and has no conditional estimation error.  If \(s\geq2\), then, conditionally on \(W_{e,i}\), that average is an order-\((s-1)\) \(U\)-statistic based on the other \(n_e-1\) observations.  After subtracting its conditional expectation, summands indexed by disjoint tuples are conditionally independent, while the number of overlapping pairs is \(O(n_e^{2s-3})\) out of \(O(n_e^{2s-2})\) pairs.  The kernel second moment is uniformly bounded by the moment envelope.  Hence, in both cases,
\[
 \mathbb E\left|
 {n_e-1\choose s-1}^{-1}
 \sum_{|J|=s-1}g(W_{e,i},W_{e,J})
 -\mathbb E[g(W_{e,i},W_2,\ldots,W_s)\mid W_{e,i}]
 \right|^2\leq K/n_e.
\]
The same overlap calculation gives
\(\mathbb E|U_{e,s}(g)-\mathbb E g|^2\leq K/n_e\).  Thus, after stacking the finitely many constituent kernels and contrast signs,
\[
 \mathbb E R_n^\psi\leq K/n,
 \qquad
 R_n^\psi=\frac1n\sum_{e,i}\pi_e^{-2}
 \|\widehat\psi_{e,i}-\psi_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\|^2.
 \tag{10}
\]
Jensen's inequality applied to the leave-one-out averages and to the \(U\)-statistics, together with \((2+\nu)R_{\max}\leq2R_{\max}+\delta\), also gives uniform \((2+\nu)\)-moment bounds for both \(\widehat\psi_{e,i}\) and \(\psi_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\).

Put \(h_k=m_k-\beta c_k\), \(\widehat h_k=\widehat m_k-\beta\widehat c_k\), and define
\[
 L_n^2=\|\widehat Q-Q_A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 +\|\widehat C^\dagger-C^+\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 +\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\|\widehat h_k-h_k\|^2.
\]
On \(\{\|\widehat C-C\|\leq\kappa_0/2\}\), the inverse identity used in the projector expansion gives
\(\|\widehat C^\dagger-C^+\|\leq K\|\widehat C-C\|\).  Off this event, the threshold in the definition gives
\(\|\widehat C^\dagger\|\leq2/\kappa_0\), while \(\|C^+\|\leq1/\kappa_0\); (7) controls the event.  The projector perturbation bound and the \(U\)-statistic mean squared errors therefore yield
\[
 \mathbb E L_n^2\leq K/n,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E L_n\leq K n^{-1/2}.
 \tag{11}
\]
Let
\[
 Y_n=1+\frac1n\sum_{e,i}\pi_e^{-2}
 \left\{\|\psi_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\|^2+
 \|\widehat\psi_{e,i}\|^2\right\},
 \qquad a=\nu/2.
\]
Convexity of \(x\mapsto x^{1+a}\), the bounds following (10), and balanced shares imply
\[
 \mathbb E Y_n^{1+a}\leq K.
 \tag{12}
\]
Expanding the two definitions of \(\widehat\zeta_{e,i}(\beta)\) and \(\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\), adding and subtracting one factor at a time, and using the uniform bounds on \(C^+\), \(\widehat C^\dagger\), and \(h_k\), gives
\[
 B_n:=\frac1n\sum_{e,i}\pi_e^{-2}
 \|\widehat\zeta_{e,i}(\beta)-\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\|^2
 \leq K\{R_n^\psi+L_n^2Y_n\}.
 \tag{13}
\]
This is an algebraic inequality; no independence between \(L_n\) and \(Y_n\) is asserted or needed.

Define the true-influence empirical covariance
\[
 \widetilde\Sigma_n=\frac1n\sum_{e,i}\pi_e^{-2}
 \zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i})\zeta_{e,n}(W_{e,i})^\top
\]
and the multiplier covariance
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)=\frac1n\sum_{e,i}\pi_e^{-2}
 \widehat\zeta_{e,i}(\beta)\widehat\zeta_{e,i}(\beta)^\top.
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz for the empirical sums, (12)--(13) imply
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)-\widetilde\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq K\{(R_n^\psi Y_n)^{1/2}+L_nY_n+R_n^\psi+L_n^2Y_n\}.
 \tag{14}
\]
We now integrate this bound directly.  For every \(t>0\), (10) and (12) give
\[
 \mathbb E[1\wedge R_n^\psi Y_n]
 \leq t\mathbb E R_n^\psi+\Pr(Y_n>t)
 \leq K\{t/n+t^{-(1+a)}\}.
\]
Taking \(t=n^{1/(2+a)}\) and then applying Jensen's inequality gives
\[
 \mathbb E[1\wedge(R_n^\psi Y_n)^{1/2}]
 \leq K n^{-\kappa},
 \qquad
 \kappa=\frac{1+a}{2(2+a)}.
 \tag{15}
\]
Similarly, without any independence assumption, (11)--(12) yield
\[
 \mathbb E[1\wedge L_nY_n]
 \leq t\mathbb E L_n+\Pr(Y_n>t)
 \leq K\{tn^{-1/2}+t^{-(1+a)}\}.
\]
Taking \(t=n^{1/\{2(2+a)\}}\) gives the same \(K n^{-\kappa}\) bound.  The terms \(R_n^\psi\) and \(L_n^2Y_n\) in (14) are faster: for the latter, taking \(t=n^{1/(2+a)}\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E[1\wedge L_n^2Y_n]
 \leq K n^{-(1+a)/(2+a)}.
\]
Consequently (14) implies the quantitative uniform-integrability bound
\[
 \sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[
 1\wedge\|\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)-\widetilde\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \right]
 \leq K n^{-\kappa}.
 \tag{16}
\]
This calculation upgrades the mean squared leave-one-out error in (10); an \(O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1})\) statement alone would not imply (16).

For completeness, we also control empirical averaging of the true influences.  Each matrix
\(\zeta_{e,n}\zeta_{e,n}^\top\) has a uniformly bounded \((1+a)\)-moment by (3).  Truncate its norm at
\[
 \ell_n=n^{1/\{2(1+a)\}}.
\]
The tail expectation is at most \(K\ell_n^{-a}\).  The mean absolute deviation of the average of the centered truncated matrices is at most its root mean square, which is bounded by
\[
 K n^{-1/2}\ell_n^{(1-a)/2}.
\]
The second term is smaller than the first for \(0<a\leq1/2\).  Since the expectation of \(\widetilde\Sigma_n\) is exactly \(\Sigma_n\), stratified independence and balanced shares give
\[
 \sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta
 \|\widetilde\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq K n^{-a/\{2(1+a)\}}
 =K n^{-\nu/(4+2\nu)}.
 \tag{17}
\]
Now
\[
 2\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}=\frac{a}{2(1+a)},
 \qquad
 \kappa-2\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}
 =\frac{1}{2(2+a)(1+a)}>0.
\]
Because \(\tau_n=n^{-\chi}\) and \(\chi<\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}\), equations (16)--(17) give both the requested replacement rate and the total covariance rate:
\[
 \sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[
 1\wedge\|\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)-\widetilde\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \right]=o(\tau_n^2),
 \tag{18}
\]
\[
 \sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[
 1\wedge\|\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)-\Sigma_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \right]
 \leq K n^{-2\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}}=o(\tau_n^2).
 \tag{19}
\]

Conditionally on the data, \(G_n^{*(j)}(\beta)\) is exactly Gaussian with covariance \(\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)\).  For positive semidefinite matrices \(S,T\), the square-root integral
\[
 S^{1/2}=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty
 t^{-1/2}S(S+tI)^{-1}\,dt
\]
and the resolvent identity, split at \(t=\|S-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), give
\[
 \|S^{1/2}-T^{1/2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq K\|S-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{1/2}.
 \tag{20}
\]
This calculation remains valid when either matrix has zero eigenvalues.  Couple the conditional multiplier Gaussian and \(N(0,\Sigma_n)\) as
\(\widehat\Sigma_n(\beta)^{1/2}Z\) and \(\Sigma_n^{1/2}Z\), with \(Z\sim N(0,I_{D_{\mathrm{AR}}})\).  Equations (19)--(20) and Jensen's inequality yield
\[
 \sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\bigl(
 \mathcal L^*(G_n^{*(j)}(\beta)),N(0,\Sigma_n)
 \bigr)
 \leq K n^{-\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}}.
 \tag{21}
\]

It remains to remove atomic discontinuities.  Let \(G_n\sim N(0,\Sigma_n)\), let \(\xi\sim N(0,1)\) be independent, and define
\[
 F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(t)
 =\Pr\{\|G_n\|_{\max}+\tau_n\xi\leq t\}.
\]
For every \(t\), the map
\[
 x\longmapsto
 \Phi\!\left(\frac{t-\|x\|_{\max}}{\tau_n}\right)
\]
is bounded by one and has Lipschitz constant at most
\((\sqrt{2\pi}\tau_n)^{-1}\).  Therefore (9), (21), and \(\chi<\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}\) imply
\[
 \sup_{\theta,t}
 \left|\Pr_\theta\{V_n(\beta)\leq t\}
 -F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(t)\right|\longrightarrow0,
 \tag{22}
\]
\[
 \sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta\sup_t
 \left|\Pr^*\{V_n^{*(j)}(\beta)\leq t\}
 -F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(t)\right|\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{23}
\]
Indeed, the bound in (22) is \(O(n^{\chi-2\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}})\), and the bound in (23) is \(O(n^{\chi-\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}})\).  Both vanish.

The ideal distribution is continuous and strictly increasing even when \(\Sigma_n\) is singular or zero, because its density is
\[
 t\longmapsto
 \mathbb E\left[
 \tau_n^{-1}\phi\!\left(
 \frac{t-\|G_n\|_{\max}}{\tau_n}
 \right)
 \right]>0.
 \tag{24}
\]
For a variable with distribution function \(F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}\), direct inversion of this strictly increasing function shows that \(1-F_{n,\theta}^{\circ}(V)\) is uniform on \((0,1)\).  Equations (22)--(23) and the elementary inverse-distribution inequalities therefore imply that the conditional upper-tail probability
\[
 p_n^*(\beta)=\Pr^*\{V_n^{*(j)}(\beta)\geq V_n(\beta)\}
\]
converges in distribution to a uniform random variable, uniformly over the shell.  The jitters make both conditional and unconditional comparison distributions continuous, so the weak inequality creates no residual tie probability.

Conditionally on the data and \(\xi_0\), the \(m_n\) indicators defining \(\widehat p_{n,m_n}(\beta)\) are independent Bernoulli variables with success probability \(p_n^*(\beta)\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(
 \widehat p_{n,m_n}(\beta)\mid\text{data},\xi_0
 \right)
 =\frac{p_n^*(\beta)\{1-p_n^*(\beta)\}}{m_n}
 \leq\frac1{4m_n}.
 \tag{25}
\]
Chebyshev's inequality and \(m_n\to\infty\) show that the Monte Carlo error is \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), uniformly.  Since \(\alpha_0\in(0,1/2)\) is a continuity point of the uniform law,
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)}
 \left|
 \Pr_\theta\{\widehat p_{n,m_n}(\beta)>\alpha_0\}
 -(1-\alpha_0)
 \right|\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{26}
\]
The probability in (26) integrates over the observations, all multiplier draws, \(\xi_0\), and all Monte Carlo jitters.  By construction, the event in (26) is exactly
\(\{\beta\in\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\}\).  This proves the uniform exact-coverage assertion.  Moreover, \(\tau_n\xi_0=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and \(\tau_n\xi_j=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) on the root-\(n\) projected-moment scale, so the calibration randomization vanishes asymptotically.

Finally, let \(F\) have an atom at \(x_0\).  The deterministic strict single-threshold rule has acceptance probability \(F(x_0-)\), and the deterministic weak single-threshold rule has acceptance probability \(F(x_0)\).  If
\(F(x_0-)<1-\alpha_0<F(x_0)\), neither equals the target.  Randomized acceptance on the equality event with probability
\[
 \frac{1-\alpha_0-F(x_0-)}{F(x_0)-F(x_0-)}
\]
does attain the target.  This proves exactly the stated limitation for deterministic single-threshold conventions and makes no broader impossibility assertion.
theorem.justification: Vanishing external Gaussian randomization converts the singular Gaussian approximation into exact, rather than conservative, null calibration without imposing an influence-covariance eigenvalue bound.
theorem.gap: The same-sample estimated-plane correction is handled by the generated-projector expansion; the additional quantitative truncation argument proves that estimated-influence covariance replacement is negligible relative to the squared jitter scale.
theorem.consumer: The construction gives protein-signaling analysts an implementable covariance-adaptive Anderson--Rubin confidence set when the environmental cumulant flag is weak or its influence covariance changes rank.

proposed.construction:
If some environment has \(n_e<R_{\max}\), define
\[
 \mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}=[-B,B]
\]
and stop: none of the \(U\)-statistics, leave-one-out projections, multipliers, or jitters below is formed.  Suppose henceforth that \(n_e\geq R_{\max}\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\).  Put
\[
 \mathcal K=\{d+2,\ldots,R_{\max}\},
 \qquad
 D_{\mathrm{AR}}=(E-1)|\mathcal K|,
 \qquad
 \|x\|_{\max}=\max_{k\in\mathcal K}\|x_k\|_2
\]
for \(x=(x_k:k\in\mathcal K)\in\mathbb R^{D_{\mathrm{AR}}}\).  Write \(W_{e,i}=(T_{e,i},Y_{e,i})\).  Each coordinate of a sample cumulant is a fixed finite linear combination of symmetric \(U\)-statistics.  For an order-\(s\) constituent with symmetric kernel \(g\) in environment \(e\), write
\[
 U_{e,s}(g)={n_e\choose s}^{-1}
 \sum_{\substack{I\subset\{1,\ldots,n_e\}\\ |I|=s}}g(W_{e,I})
\]
and define its leave-one-out first-projection estimate by
\[
 \widehat\psi_{g,e,i}
 =s\left[
 {n_e-1\choose s-1}^{-1}
 \sum_{\substack{J\subset\{1,\ldots,n_e\}\setminus\{i\}\\ |J|=s-1}}
 g\bigl(W_{e,i},W_{e,J}\bigr)-U_{e,s}(g)
 \right].
\]
Apply the same finite linear combinations and the same environment-versus-baseline contrast signs as in \(\widehat C\), \(\widehat c_k\), and \(\widehat m_k\) to obtain \(\widehat\psi^C_{e,i}\), \(\widehat\psi^c_{e,k,i}\), and \(\widehat\psi^m_{e,k,i}\).  Define
\[
 \widehat C^\dagger=
 \begin{cases}
  (\widehat C^\top\widehat C)^{-1}\widehat C^\top,
    &\sigma_d(\widehat C)\geq\kappa_0/2,\\
  0,&\sigma_d(\widehat C)<\kappa_0/2,
 \end{cases}
\]
and, for \(b\in[-B,B]\),
\[
 \widehat h_k(b)=\widehat m_k-b\widehat c_k,
 \qquad
 \widehat\zeta_{e,k,i}(b)
 =\widehat Q\left\{
 \widehat\psi^m_{e,k,i}-b\widehat\psi^c_{e,k,i}
 -\widehat\psi^C_{e,i}\widehat C^\dagger\widehat h_k(b)
 \right\}.
\]
Let \(\widehat\zeta_{e,i}(b)\in\mathbb R^{D_{\mathrm{AR}}}\) stack these vectors over \(k\in\mathcal K\), and put
\[
 H_n(b)=\left(
 \sqrt n\,\widehat Q(\widehat m_k-b\widehat c_k):k\in\mathcal K
 \right).
\]
Set
\[
 \nu=\min\{1,\delta/R_{\max}\},
 \qquad
 \varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}=\frac{\nu}{8+4\nu}.
\]
Choose \(0<\chi<\varrho_{\mathrm{AR}}\), put \(\tau_n=n^{-\chi}\), and choose a deterministic integer sequence \(m_n\to\infty\).  Independently of the data, draw mutually independent standard normal variables
\[
 \{\omega^{(j)}_{e,i}:e\in\mathcal E,\ 1\leq i\leq n_e,
 1\leq j\leq m_n\}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \xi_0,\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_{m_n}.
\]
For every \(b\in[-B,B]\), form
\[
 G_n^{*(j)}(b)=\frac1{\sqrt n}
 \sum_{e\in\mathcal E}\sum_{i=1}^{n_e}
 \pi_e^{-1}\widehat\zeta_{e,i}(b)\omega^{(j)}_{e,i},
\]
\[
 V_n(b)=\|H_n(b)\|_{\max}+\tau_n\xi_0,
 \qquad
 V_n^{*(j)}(b)=\|G_n^{*(j)}(b)\|_{\max}+\tau_n\xi_j,
\]
and
\[
 \widehat p_{n,m_n}(b)=\frac1{m_n}\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}
 \mathbf 1\{V_n^{*(j)}(b)\geq V_n(b)\}.
\]
The randomized-jitter Gaussian-multiplier Anderson--Rubin inversion is
\[
 \mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}
 =\{b\in[-B,B]:\widehat p_{n,m_n}(b)>\alpha_0\}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: Adds the complete implementable multiplier, estimated-influence, Gaussian-jitter, Monte Carlo, and inversion map, with the small-sample fallback evaluated before any undefined statistic.

prose_updates.tldr: Simultaneous changes in latent and treatment noises create an exact source-label ambiguity.  When environment-indexed latent cumulant shifts occupy an unknown calibrated \(d\)-plane, the orthogonal flag \(Q_Ac_k\) identifies \(\beta\) at its first nonzero order, while global absence of a flag admits a legal unequal-effect source swap.  The environment threshold \(E=d+2\), every first identifying order, and the weak-breakout estimation and honest-length rates are sharp on the stated domains.  The same-sample estimated-plane influence expansion now also yields an implementable Gaussian-multiplier Anderson--Rubin inversion: vanishing Gaussian jitter gives asymptotically exact unconditional coverage uniformly through singular, rank-changing, and zero influence covariance.

project_justification.fill: The project gives an if-and-only-if observed-law frontier, an explicit compatible-bounds construction proving that its no-breakout branch contains interior unequal-effect laws, a sharp \(d+2\) environment threshold, realizable lower-order-indistinguishable models at every cumulant order, universal rate upper bounds, matching lower bounds on one compatible experiment, a uniform generated-projector expansion, and a covariance-adaptive Gaussian-multiplier Anderson--Rubin inversion whose vanishing jitter handles atomic critical laws.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cumulants through \(R_{\max}\) are estimated by symmetrized \(U\)-statistics, \(A\) by the rank-\(d\) SVD of \(\widehat C\), and the projected-moment influence covariance by leave-one-out first projections.  Independent Gaussian multipliers and vanishing Gaussian jitters provide the covariance-adaptive Anderson--Rubin calibration; reported coverage integrates over all auxiliary draws.

prose_updates.related_work: Kivva, Akbari, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (2025), especially Theorem 3.6 and its source-swap proof, supply the closest obstruction and the mixed-cumulant algebra; their local analytic-mgf antecedent is weaker than the globally finite-mgf restriction maintained here.  The present target answers their stated multi-environment question under a new low-rank profile restriction and is positioned as informed by, rather than as a strict tightening of, that theorem.  Rothenhäusler, Heinze, Peters, and Meinshausen (2015) give BACKSHIFT's contrasting covariance joint-diagonalization condition; that paper does not support the present loading, calibration-rank, or calibration-gap restrictions.  Cai et al. (2023), Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025), and Tramontano et al. (2025) demonstrate higher-cumulant recovery under one-latent-component, targeted-intervention, proxy, or instrumental structure; none supplies the environmental source-label frontier here.  Li, Kwok, Guo, and Liu (2026) characterize effect identifiability from one bivariate law according to noise Gaussianity and publicly exclude constrained multi-environment settings from scope; the complete proof text was externally inaccessible during this scan, so the paper is treated only as an informed-by comparator.  Long et al. (2023) provide the environmental GMM template in a regular supplied-moment model.  Andrews and Guggenberger (2019) provide singularity-robust Anderson--Rubin inference for high-level supplied moments and do not support the primitive source moment envelope or the same-sample cumulant-plane correction.  Davis and Kahan (1970) are cited solely for stability of an estimated spectral projector under matrix perturbation.  Causal Dantzig supplies regular covariance-shift inference.  None of these results supplies the present leave-one-out covariance replacement bound or the vanishing-jitter calibration through zero and rank-changing influence covariance.  Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen (2020) explain why unknown intervention targets, latent confounding, and feedback are material in the Sachs application, while Sachs et al. (2005) provide the multi-perturbation single-cell setting rather than evidence that the new latent-profile condition holds.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The covariance-adaptive Anderson--Rubin result is asymptotic, fixed-dimensional, and uses the maintained \(2R_{\max}+\delta\) moment envelope, the fixed calibration gap, leave-one-out influence estimates, a diverging number of Monte Carlo draws, and external Gaussian jitter.  It permits singular, rank-changing, and zero influence covariance but does not promise finite-sample exactness, conditional-on-randomization coverage, or exact deterministic threshold calibration at an atom.  The full-observation minimax lower-bound family remains established on one fixed compatible bounded experiment, not on every arbitrary nonempty bounded shell.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The identification if-and-only-if is confined to the explicitly source-labelled union \(\mathcal D_\rho\), not arbitrary simultaneous shifts.  The explicit no-breakout construction proves nonemptiness only for fixed bounds admitting positive model constants that satisfy the displayed interior, singular-gap, and moment inequalities; incompatible bounds carry no nonemptiness claim.  The entire-mgf condition is newly maintained here as a strict global strengthening of the local analytic-mgf antecedent used by Kivva et al.  The \(d=1,E=2\) reduction is already known from Kivva et al., Theorem 3.6, and the no-breakout honest-length proposition is an incremental standard consequence.  A failed finite scan through \(R_{\max}\) does not establish global no-breakout outside this domain.  The Sachs data motivate the consumer but do not verify the structural restrictions.  The original deterministic-radius Anderson--Rubin interval remains the finite-sample conservative guarantee.  The Gaussian-multiplier refinement has asymptotically exact unconditional coverage over the declared first-breakout shells because its auxiliary jitter vanishes; without such randomization, strict and weak deterministic single-threshold rules need not attain an intermediate nominal probability at an atom.
